_meta.role: lens-B re-audit of outputs/detection_engine_angle.json (axis 3 = angle dependence). Numbers of the original verdict are taken as given; only the INFERENCE is under test.
_meta.question: Does the angle axis actually decide detection, and is there a hidden angle axis where PathSolver wins?
_meta.note: outputs/detection_engine_angle.json (the audited verdict) was NOT modified; this is a separate file.

verdict.one_line: The winner survives and is in fact UNDER-argued - the project's own constant-sigma control shows that 100% of the angle dependence of the detection answer comes from sigma(aspect). What must be corrected is the axis's PURCHASING POWER, not its winner.

A_attack_that_FAILED_geometry_not_target.hypothesis: The angle dependence that moves Pd is bistatic geometry (R1/R2 spread, scene azimuth phi), not target aspect - and geometry needs no scattering engine, so the axis cannot pick an engine.
A_attack_that_FAILED_geometry_not_target.result: REFUTED by the repo's own pre-existing control arm.

evidence.ledger_headline_quote: The large phi dependence one actually sees in a raw R90-vs-phi plot (up to 28 dB-equivalent) is the drone's RCS ASPECT pattern, not geometry: it vanishes in both the constant-sigma control and the heading-averaged arm.

A_attack_that_FAILED_geometry_not_target.consequence: If the engine cannot produce sigma(aspect), the modelled detection range has essentially NO angle dependence at all (geometry alone gives 0.5%). Sionna's measured azimuth span (1.281 dB, facet_count.json) maps to R90 x1.077. Ours maps to x3.96. That is the axis, and it goes to ours.

heading_polar_R90_spread.src: outputs/report13_freespace.json :: solve[mode].heading_polar (s1000plus, L=500 m, alt=60 m, phi=90)
heading_polar_R90_spread.reads: 72 headings, same target, same range: detection range moves ~3x. Independent of the facet_count 4-azimuth cell the original verdict leaned on.

ranking_instability_is_itself_an_angle_f.reads: with angle-resolved sigma the W/L/G ranking is not stable over scene azimuth; with constant sigma it is a single order. Only an engine that produces sigma(aspect) can discover this.

C1_zero_leverage_in_the_5G_headline_mode.reads: In G1 every one of the 72 headings is Doppler-blind, so C = 0 at every range no matter what sigma(azimuth) says. In that mode the angle axis has exactly zero leverage on the detection deliverable. In W1/L1 the coverage CEILING is set by the blind sector (C_max = 1 - blind_frac exactly), and sigma(aspect) only sets where the roll-off happens.

C2_bistatic_transport_of_the_lobes.production_path: sigma grid = rcs_sbr_batch MONOSTATIC backscatter; the bistatic arm looks it up along the BISECTOR
C2_bistatic_transport_of_the_lobes.honest_reading: At the headline operating point (L=500 m, R90 ~10 km) beta is ~3 deg, inside the literature 15-20 deg validity window (outputs/injection_verdict.json flags that window), so the shortcut is probably benign THERE - but the ledger has no row between beta=0 and beta=15, so the error at 3-7 deg is NOT measured. At short range / long baseline (half the d-grid is beta>20 deg) the delivered sigma(angle) carries 6.4-8.8 dB RMS, i.e. x1.5-1.9 in R90, against the x2.9-4.0 aspect effect being sold.

and_the_error_bar_is_currently_missing.quote: report13_sigma_grid.json top keys = ['meta','sigma','sigma_confidence'] - 'multistatic' block ABSENT. meta.multistatic_regenerated=false
and_the_error_bar_is_currently_missing.kernel_state: rcs_sbr.rcs_sbr_multistatic() exists (src/rcs_sbr.py:545) and reduces to monostatic at beta=0 (benchmark/das_fleet_verify.py V1) - the CAPABILITY is there, the LEDGER is not
and_the_error_bar_is_currently_missing.reads: So today the bistatic sigma error bar quoted in geometry_grid.json belongs to an older (07-29 mesh) grid. For the current grid the number is: unknown.

C3_the_elevation_half_of_sigma_az_el_is_.denominator: not established from the ledger - I do not know the total lookup count per phi row, so I cannot state a clamped FRACTION
C3_the_elevation_half_of_sigma_az_el_is_.reads: The axis is sold as sigma(azimuth, ELEVATION). The azimuth half is dense (3 deg); the elevation half is a 0..-20 deg band that the bistatic bisector leaves often enough that the ledger keeps a counter for it.

C4_only_envelope_statistics_are_quotable.restates: the original verdict's own caveat 3, which I confirm rather than overturn
C4_only_envelope_statistics_are_quotable.numbers: PO vs SBR disagree by 19.8 dB at az=0 (facet_count.json); div=16 dither floor 1.782 dB p-p on a PEC sphere (sbr_grid_convergence.json), drone dither unmeasured; 20x decimation moves ours 0.4-2.3 dB
C4_only_envelope_statistics_are_quotable.consequence: the product is p10/p50/p90, ptp, epsilon - not a null position. The project's own recommended configuration (sigma_robust_summary.json paper_ready) is aspect_avg_anchored, i.e. the headline deliberately averages the lobes away.

D_hidden_axis_where_the_other_engine_win.name: angle dependence of the PROPAGATION, not of the target
D_hidden_axis_where_the_other_engine_win.why_it_is_not_this_axis: it does not change the winner of axis (3); it bounds what winning axis (3) buys

evidence.ledger_note_verbatim: FS-3 companion; free space is NOT an upper bound (F4 in [-20,+11.5] dB)
evidence.reads: a 31.5 dB grazing-angle-dependent term that the headline free-space chain excludes; our PO/SBR kernel is free-space and produces none of it
when the environment was actually traced (RT), the floor return was 16.2 dB stronger than the analytic stand-in. RT corrected an analytic assumption, not the other way round.

evidence.sigma_form: ONE SCALAR, no angle at all
evidence.reads: In the one place in this repo where a detection verdict actually flipped because of geometry (5G false-alarm probability 1.0), the angle-dependent quantity came from Sionna RT and our kernel contributed a single angle-free scalar. That is the exact mirror image of axis (3).

D_hidden_axis_where_the_other_engine_win.conclusion: For detection the SNR numerator is sigma(aspect) x propagation(geometry). Ours owns the first factor (PathSolver cannot produce it - confirmed, no aperture term, size-blind). RT owns the second (ours cannot produce it - free space, no environment). A single-winner verdict on 'angle dependence' is a scoping artefact; the deployable answer is composition (h = h_bg from RT + h_target from our sigma), which is also what the prior-work census records as mainstream.

E_what_I_could_not_check: Whether the bisector approximation is acceptable at beta = 3-7 deg (the actual operating point): the error ledger has rows at beta = 0 and 15 deg and nothing between. Unknown.
The clamped-lookup FRACTION in elevation (numerator known, denominator not in the ledger).
Whether the outdoor measurement geometry (X410, field test) will sit at small beta like the L=500 m headline scene. Not established anywhere I read.
Sionna diffuse-channel ABSOLUTE level with our production materials (same gap the original verdict declared; S is a free handle, 15.8 dB of swing in rt_no_rcs_verify.json B_sphere_S).

Whether the hovering / blade-line chain consumes sigma(aspect) at all: md_range_sweep.json is monostatic az=0, el=15 and reports aspect only as a 36-azimuth MEAN correction (d_sigma_aspect_mean_db). I did not find an aspect-resolved blade-line detection deliverable.
